solution: $\tan x>\cot x\iff\dfrac{\tan^2x-1}{\tan x}>0\iff\tan x>1$ or $-1<\tan x<0$
solution_full: First inequality: $2\sin^2x-3\sin x+1=(2\sin x-1)(\sin x-1)<0$. Since $\sin x-1\le0$, this needs $\sin x\ne1$ and $2\sin x-1>0$, i.e. $\frac12<\sin x<1$.
Second inequality: with $t=\tan x$ ($t\ne0$), $t>\frac1t\iff\frac{t^2-1}{t}>0\iff(t-1)(t+1)t>0\iff t>1$ or $-1<t<0$.
On $\left(\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ the tangent is positive, so we need $\tan x>1$, i.e. $x\in\left(\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

On $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)$ the tangent is negative and increases from $-\infty$ to $-\frac{1}{\sqrt3}$; we need $-1<\tan x<0$, i.e. $x\in\left(\frac{3\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)$.
Reading $\tan x>\cot x$ as $\tan^2x>1$ (multiplying by $\tan x$ without its sign) keeps only the first interval and gives $\frac{\pi}{4}$, option (A).
originality_note: New: a quadratic inequality in sin x restricts x to (pi/6, 5pi/6) and the second inequality tan x > cot x must be solved separately on each side of pi/2, where the sign of tan x reverses the inequality (way 5). Closest known: solving tan x > cot x alone (solver pages) or 2 sin^2 x - 3 sin x + 1 = 0 as an equation. Different because: the system intersects the two and the second-quadrant piece is the trap.

concept_use.Trigonometric inequalities: Each inequality is solved on its own: (2 sin x - 1)(sin x - 1) < 0 and (tan^2 x - 1)/tan x > 0.
concept_use.System of trigonometric inequalities: The two solution sets are intersected on (pi/6, pi/2) and (pi/2, 5pi/6) separately, giving (pi/4, pi/2) and (3pi/4, 5pi/6).

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, function and interval is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath (and a numerical scan), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Stated that tan x and cot x must be defined, so the points pi/2, pi, 0 are excluded without argument. Changed: added 'for which tan x and cot x are defined'.
key_step: Intersecting the sin-interval with tan x > cot x while keeping track of the sign of tan x in the second quadrant.
justification: Two inequalities each needing a genuine sign check, linked by an intersection with a reversal trap in the second quadrant; options hold the tempting pi/4. Comparable to the solution-counting items of 2026-P1-Q14 (L3).
